title: Honour shown by a sound life
source_text: Ὅτι δὲ ἡ πρὸς τὸν (υἱὸν τοῦ) θεοῦ τιμὴ ἐν βίῳ ὑγιεῖ γίνεται. οὕτως δὲ καὶ ἡ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πατέρα, ὅρα εἰ μὴ διδασκόμεθα ἔκ τε τοῦ „ὃς ἐν νόμῳ καυχᾶσαι, διὰ τῆς παραβάσεως, (τοῦ νόμου) τὸν θεὸν ἀτιμάζεις“ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ „πόσῳ δοκεῖτε χείρονος ἀξιωθήσεται τιμωρίας ὁ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καταπατήσας καὶ τὸ αἷμα τῆς διαθήκης κοινὸν ἡγησάμενος, ἐν ᾧ ἡγιάσθη, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίσας.“ εἰ γὰρ „διὰ τῆς παραβάσεως τοῦ νόμου“ ἀτιμάζει τὸν θεὸν ὁ παραβαίνων τὸν νόμον, καὶ καταπατεῖ „τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ“ ὁ μὴ καταπατῶν τὸν λόγον· δῆλον ὅτι τιμᾷ μὲν τὸν θεὸν ὁ τηρῶν τὸν νόμον, σέβει δὲ τὸν θεὸν ὁ κεκοσμημένος τῷ λόγῳ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῖς ἔργοις αὐτοῦ. εἰ δὲ ᾔδει Κέλσος, τίνες μέν εἰσι τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ὅτι μόνοι οἱ σοφοὶ, τίνες δὲ οἱ ἀλλότριοι, καὶ ὅτι πάντες οἱ φαῦλοι οἱ μηδαμῶς νεύοντες πρὸς ἀρετῆς ἀνάληψιν. εἶδεν ἂν, πῶς δεῖ (λέγειν) τὸ τιμῶν οὖν τις καὶ σέβων τοὺς ἐκείνου πάντας τί λυπεῖ τὸν θεὸν, οὗ πάντες εἰσίν;
pass_a_gloss: That the honour (τιμή) toward the Son of God comes about in a sound life (ἐν βίῳ ὑγιεῖ), and so also that toward God and Father, see if we are not taught both from 'you who boast (καυχᾶσαι) in the law, through the transgression (παράβασις) of the law you dishonour (ἀτιμάζεις) God' and from 'by how much worse punishment (τιμωρία) do you think will be deemed worthy the one who trampled underfoot (καταπατήσας) the Son of God and regarded as common (κοινόν) the blood of the covenant (διαθήκη) in which he was sanctified (ἡγιάσθη), and insulted (ἐνυβρίσας) the Spirit of grace (χάρις).' For if 'through the transgression of the law' the one transgressing the law dishonours God, and the one [μὴ, transmitted] trampling the Word (λόγος) tramples 'the Son of God', it is clear that the one keeping (τηρῶν) the law honours God, and the one adorned (κεκοσμημένος) with the Word of God and His works (ἔργοις) reveres (σέβει) God. But if Celsus had known who are of God, and that [they are] the wise (σοφοί) alone, and who are the strangers (ἀλλότριοι), and that [they are] all the wicked (φαῦλοι) who in no way incline (νεύοντες) toward the taking up (ἀνάληψις) of virtue (ἀρετή), he would have seen how one must (δεῖ) say 'honouring then and revering (σέβων) all who are His, how does one grieve (λυπεῖ) God, whose all are?'
pass_b_english: See whether we are not taught that honour toward the Son of God, and in the same way honour toward God the Father, is rendered through a sound life, both from the words “You who boast in the law dishonour God by breaking the law” (Romans 2:23), and from these: “How much worse a punishment, do you think, will be deserved by the one who has trampled underfoot the Son of God, and has counted as common the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?” (Hebrews 10:29). For if the one who breaks the law dishonours God “by breaking the law” (Romans 2:23), and the one who tramples on the Word tramples underfoot “the Son of God” (Hebrews 10:29), it is plain that the one who keeps the law honours God, and the one who is adorned with the Word of God and with His works reveres God.

If Celsus had known who belong to God, namely the wise alone, and who are strangers to Him, namely all the wicked who show no inclination at all to take up virtue, he would have seen in what sense one ought to say his words: “If then one honours and reveres all who are His, how does he grieve God, to whom they all belong?”

choices.choice: Doubtful reading: the copy-text has ὁ μὴ καταπατῶν τὸν λόγον (‘the one who does NOT trample the Word’); the Perseus TEI of Koetschau (books/ante-nicene-topics/sources/greek/origen_celsum.xml, line 18114) and the working Greek both carry μή, so it is not a staging error. It contradicts the argument (the parallel is: transgressor dishonours God; trampler of the Word tramples the Son). Rendered by sense as ‘the one who tramples on the Word’; the printed Koetschau page and apparatus have not been checked. The supplements in parentheses (υἱὸν τοῦ, τοῦ νόμου, λέγειν) are editorial and are translated. Romans 2:23 is quoted with ‘through transgression’ before the verb; rendered in natural English order. ‘Word’ is capitalised because Origen ties the trampled λόγος to the Son of God in Hebrews 10:29. ‘His works’ keeps the ambiguous αὐτοῦ (the Word’s or God’s). Celsus’s closing words come from 8.2 (‘all are His’).
'is shown in a sound life' -> 'is rendered through a sound life' (γίνεται: honour is paid, not displayed)
'who in no way incline toward taking up virtue' -> 'who show no inclination at all to take up virtue' (natural order, μηδαμῶς kept)
'how one ought to say his words' -> 'in what sense one ought to say his words' (πῶς δεῖ λέγειν)
translator note: recorded that the raw TEI itself carries μή (line 18114)
